quiz.question: 1. Why must a project establish a baseline?
options: A. To make the report longer
B. To compare the candidate against a known reference under equivalent conditions
C. To guarantee the candidate is faster
quiz.explanation: A baseline (such as a single-threaded version or standard mutex) provides a scientific point of comparison. Without a controlled baseline tested under equivalent conditions, performance claims are meaningless.

quiz.question: 2. Which statement about concurrency testing is correct?
options: A. One successful run proves race freedom
B. ThreadSanitizer finds every possible concurrency bug
C. Stress tests and race detectors provide useful evidence but cannot prove all behavior correct
quiz.explanation: Concurrency bugs are non-deterministic. While ThreadSanitizer and stress tests provide strong empirical evidence, they explore only executed execution interleavings and cannot mathematically prove the absence of all races.

quiz.question: 3. What should a benchmark report include?
options: B. The workload, environment, methodology, repeated measurements, and limitations
C. Only a screenshot of a terminal
quiz.explanation: Rigorous systems benchmarking requires recording hardware topology, kernel version, compiler flags, fixed workloads, warm-up runs, median results, tail latency (p95/p99), and measurement variances.

quiz.question: 4. A component fails when its queue reaches capacity. What should its design specify?
options: A. A documented full-queue policy and test cases
B. Nothing if the queue is usually empty
C. That the error can be ignored
quiz.explanation: Failure handling is an explicit part of interface design. A bounded queue contract must document whether full queues block, drop oldest, reject with an error code (backpressure), or signal an event.

quiz.question: 5. What makes the capstone portfolio-ready?
options: A. A large codebase regardless of quality
B. A working implementation supported by tests, benchmarks, documentation, and a reproducible demonstration
C. A presentation without source code
quiz.explanation: Distinguished engineering portfolios demonstrate verified correctness, comprehensive automated testing, reproducible benchmark results, documented design trade-offs, and clear technical communication.

theorySections.title: Design, Implement, Benchmark, and Defend a Complete Systems Component
paragraphs: This is the final milestone of the PrepSpaces Operating Systems Engineering curriculum. You will synthesize CPU scheduling, virtual memory, concurrency, filesystems, networking, and performance diagnostics to build an end-to-end systems component supported by repeatable benchmarks, ThreadSanitizer verification, and a professional engineering report.

theorySections.title: Select Your Approved Capstone Project Track
paragraphs: Choose one project track matching your interests and hardware constraints. Project C (Concurrent Worker Queue) is the recommended default for multicore concurrency, while Project G is ideal for kernel-focused portfolios.

theorySections.title: The 7-Phase Systems Engineering Workflow
paragraphs: Follow the structured lifecycle used in industrial systems development: from initial problem framing through correctness verification and benchmark defense.

theorySections.title: Bounded Worker Queue & Explicit Backpressure Engine
paragraphs: Unbounded queues cause memory exhaustion and catastrophic latency spikes. A production systems queue enforces a rigid capacity bound \(C\) and defines deterministic behavior when full: blocking producers or rejecting with an error (backpressure).
Observe condition variable signaling and backpressure activation when capacity is exhausted.

theorySections.title: Performance Benchmarking & Tail Latency Distributions
paragraphs: Systems performance is not a single number. Engineers must report median throughput alongside tail latency percentiles (p50, p95, p99) to detect lock contention queuing cliffs.
Compare Single-Threaded Baseline vs POSIX Mutex vs Lock-Free Atomic CAS across thread counts.

theorySections.title: Standard Systems Repository Layout & Build Reproducibility
paragraphs: A professional systems submission must be clean, structured, and immediately reproducible by an independent evaluator on standard Linux environments.

theorySections.title: Capstone Submission Deliverables & Portfolio Readiness
paragraphs: The 9 mandatory portfolio deliverables. Track your completion progress before submitting.

theorySections.title: Operating Systems Engineering Capstone Report & Assessment Rubric
paragraphs: Evaluators grade capstone submissions against a 100-point rubric focusing on engineering evidence, verified invariants, and rigorous failure analysis.
